sentences.text: This fourth application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.77/2020 registered at Police Station Nai Mandi Gharsana, District Sriganganagar for the offence punishable under Sections 498A and 306 IPC.
As per prosecution, on 19.3.2020 the deceased Anju Rani committed suicide by hanging herself.
As per prosecution, deceased was being harassed and humiliated by the petitioner and his family members in connection with the demand of dowry.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the marriage of the deceased with the present petitioner was solemnized 8 years before the date when deceased committed suicide.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that till date, out of 22 prosecution witnesses, 6 have been examined viz. P.W.1 Sandeep [2023/RJJD/015580] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-1463/2023] Kumar (complainant), P.W. 2 Parmeshwari Devi (mother of the deceased), P.W. 3 Vinod Kumar, P.W.4 Kesararam, P.W.5 Chanan Ram and P.W.6 Sahib Ram.

Learned counsel submitted that from perusal of the statements of these witnesses, it is evident that there is no allegation of demand of Hansraj vs State Of Rajasthan (2023/Rjjd/015580) on 16 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148839908/
1 dowry by the petitioner soon before the death of the deceased.
Learned counsel further submitted that no details whatsoever has been mentioned by the witnesses to substantiate the allegation of demand of dowry.

Lastly, learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently submitted that there exists no evidence showing that the deceased was meted out with the continuous harassment or by any action of the petitioner, deceased could be said to have been compelled to commit suicide.

Learned counsel submitted that even if the allegation of wrongdoings/abusing behaviour or harassment are taken on their face value, then also the prosecution is required to establish a positive act on the part of the accused to instigate or abet the deceased in committing suicide.
Learned counsel submitted that the trial is likely to take sufficiently long time and hence, the petitioner deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner as also the learned Public Prosecutor and perused the material available on record.

Hon'ble the Apex court in M. Arjuna vs. State, represented by its Inspector of Police, reported in (2019) 3 SCC 315, pleased to hold as under:-
[2023/RJJD/015580] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-1463/2023] "The essential ingredients of the offence under Section 306 I.P.C. are: (i) the abetment, (ii) the intention of the accused to aid or instigate or abet the deceased to commit suicide.

entities.text: M. Arjuna vs. State, represented by its Inspector of Police, reported in (2019) 3 SCC 315
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The act of the accused, however, insulting the deceased by using abusive language will not, by itself,
constitute the abetment of suicide.
There should be evidence capable of suggesting that the accused intended by such act to instigate the deceased to commit suicide.

Unless the ingredients of instigation/abetment to commit suicide are satisfied,
accused cannot be convicted under Section 306 I.P.C."

Having considered the submissions advanced at the bar and having gone through the facts and circumstances of the case so also the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses recorded before competent criminal court till date, prima-facie this Court does not find sufficient evidence to indicate that the petitioner is guilty of the act of instigation of the act of suicide, in the opinion of this Court, the petitioner deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Consequently, the fourth application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner - Hansraj S/o Sh. Shera Ram arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.77/2020 registered at Police Station Nai Mandi Gharsana, District Sriganganagar shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
